scope.beginning: The episode begins with Gaia already formed as earth but lacking the sky above her.
scope.ending: It ends when Uranus covers Gaia and becomes the partner from whom later divine children descend.

narrative.synopsis: Gaia, newly present as earth, brings forth the starry Uranus to cover her on every side. She also produces mountains and sea, and the earth-sky pairing becomes the foundation for the first divine household.
narrative.openingSituation: Gaia exists before the sky has taken its place above her.
narrative.centralConflict: The world needs height, horizon, and surrounding waters before divine generations can unfold.
narrative.resolution: Uranus stretches over Gaia, while mountains and Pontus complete the first landscape.
narrative.outcome: Earth and sky are joined, setting up both creation and later oppression.

events.consequence: The starry sky comes from Gaia.
Mountains give the earth visible height.
The sea takes its place around the land.
Their union prepares the next generation.
